Constrained shortest path

Source: R/routing.R
ox_route_constrained.Rd

Finds the minimum-weight route from from to to whose total consumption of a second edge column (resource) does not exceed budget — e.g. "the shortest route using at most 500 m of residential streets", with the residential metres counted by ox_add_edge_penalties(). This is the classic constrained shortest path problem.

Usage

ox_route_constrained(
  g,
  from,
  to,
  weight = "length",
  resource,
  budget,
  method = c("exact", "lagrangian")
)

Arguments

g

An osm_graph.

from, to

Node osmids (as returned by ox_nearest_nodes()).

weight

Edge column used as routing cost. Default "length".

resource

Name of a nonnegative edge column holding the second criterion, e.g. the "penalty" column of ox_add_edge_penalties().

budget

Maximum total resource the route may consume.

method

"exact" (default) or "lagrangian"; see Details.

Value

A one-row sf tibble: cost, resource, lower_bound (a proven lower bound on the optimal cost; equals cost whenever optimality is certified, which is always the case for method = "exact"), a list-column path of the node osmids traversed, and the route's merged street geometry. An error is raised when no route fits the budget (the message reports the minimum feasible resource).

Details

Two solvers, both in the Rust core:

  • method = "exact" (default) — bicriteria label-setting; always returns the true optimum (see ox_route_pareto() for the machinery and for the full cost-vs-resource trade-off curve).

  • method = "lagrangian" — Lagrangian relaxation (the LARAC algorithm): the budget constraint is dualized, so each iteration is a plain Dijkstra on weight + lambda * resource, with a binary search driving lambda to the dual optimum. It scales to networks where the exact front grows too large, at the price of a possible duality gap: the route is always feasible, and lower_bound brackets how far from optimal it can be (cost == lower_bound proves optimality; a message reports any gap).

Examples

g <- example_osm_graph()
g$edges$highway <- ifelse(abs(g$edges$u - g$edges$v) == 1, "residential", "primary")
g <- ox_add_edge_penalties(g, c(residential = 1))
from <- ox_nearest_nodes(g, 0, 0)
to <- ox_nearest_nodes(g, 300, 300)
# shortest route crossing at most 300 m of residential streets
ox_route_constrained(g, from, to, resource = "penalty", budget = 300)
#> Simple feature collection with 1 feature and 4 fields
#> Geometry type: LINESTRING
#> Dimension:     XY
#> Bounding box:  xmin: 0 ymin: 0 xmax: 300 ymax: 300
#> Projected CRS: WGS 84 / Pseudo-Mercator
#> # A tibble: 1 × 5
#>    cost resource lower_bound path                                       geometry
#>   <dbl>    <dbl>       <dbl> <list>                             <LINESTRING [m]>
#> 1   600      300         600 <int [7]> (0 0, 100 0, 200 0, 200 100, 300 100, 30…
ox_route_constrained(g, from, to, resource = "penalty", budget = 300,
                     method = "lagrangian")
#> Simple feature collection with 1 feature and 4 fields
#> Geometry type: LINESTRING
#> Dimension:     XY
#> Bounding box:  xmin: 0 ymin: 0 xmax: 300 ymax: 300
